where
  homEquiv :=
    { toFun φ := (Subobject.pullback φ).obj 𝒞.truth_as_subobject
      invFun x := 𝒞.χ x.arrow
      left_inv φ := by simp
      right_inv x := by simp }
  homEquiv_comp _ _ := by simp [pullback_comp]
result.informal_name: Representability of the Subobject Presheaf by the Classifier Ω
result.informal_description: In a category $\mathcal{C}$ with pullbacks and a subobject classifier $\Omega_\mathcal{C}$, the subobject presheaf $\text{Sub}(X)$ is naturally isomorphic to the hom-functor $\text{Hom}(-, \Omega_\mathcal{C})$. Specifically, for every object $X$, there is a natural bijection between subobjects of $X$ and morphisms $X \to \Omega_\mathcal{C}$, given by pulling back the truth subobject $\text{truth}: \Omega_0 \to \Omega_\mathcal{C}$ along the characteristic morphism $\chi$. This establishes that $\Omega_\mathcal{C}$ universally classifies subobjects via pullbacks.

result.informal_name: Equivalence between Subobject Classifier and Representable Subobject Presheaf
result.informal_description: In a category $\mathcal{C}$ with pullbacks, the existence of a subobject classifier is equivalent to the contravariant subobject presheaf $\text{Subobject}(-)$ being representable. Specifically, $\mathcal{C}$ has a subobject classifier if and only if there exists an object $\Omega$ such that the subobject presheaf is naturally isomorphic to the Hom functor $\text{Hom}(-, \Omega)$.

result.informal_name: Equality of Subobject Classifiers Implies Equality of Representability Data
result.informal_description: In a category $\mathcal{C}$ with pullbacks, if two objects $\Omega$ and $\Omega_1$ are equal, then the data witnessing that the subobject presheaf is representable by $\Omega$ is equal to the data witnessing representability by $\Omega_1$. Formally, $\Omega = \Omega_1$ implies $\text{SubobjectRepresentableBy}\,\Omega = \text{SubobjectRepresentableBy}\,\Omega_1$.

name: ComputablePred
computable_iff
result.signature: {p : α → Prop} : ComputablePred p ↔ ∃ f : α → Bool, Computable f ∧ p = fun a => (f a : Prop)
result.type: ∀ {α : Type u_1} [inst : Primcodable α] {p : α → Prop}, ComputablePred p ↔ ∃ f, Computable f ∧ p = fun a => f a = true
result.informal_name: A predicate is computable if and only if it is represented by a computable boolean function
result.informal_description: For a predicate $ p $ on a primcodable type $ \alpha $, the predicate $ p $ is computable if and only if there exists a computable function $ f : \alpha \to \mathsf{Bool} $ such that $ p(a) $ holds precisely when $ f(a) $ evaluates to true.

This structure enables the classification of subobjects via pullbacks, ensuring that every monomorphism arises as the pullback of $\text{truth}$ along a unique characteristic morphism.

result.informal_name: Congruence of Classifying Morphism for Subobject Classifier
result.informal_description: In a category $\mathcal{C}$ with pullbacks and a subobject classifier $\Omega$, if two representations $h$ and $h_1$ of the subobject classifier are equal, then for any subobject $m: A \to X$ (with $m = m_1$), the corresponding classifying morphisms $\chi_h(m)$ and $\chi_{h_1}(m_1)$ are equal. This expresses that the classifying morphism $\chi$ is uniquely determined by the subobject and the representable structure.
